scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic element count multiplied in a wider mathematical domain truncates before allocation while the downstream consumer still uses the wider logical count.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A fake allocator and controlled shadow-range consumer record only requested size, usable size, logical count, and inert range receipts without real out-of-bounds access.
scenarios.positive_control: The same synthetic count multiplied with checked wide arithmetic requests exactly the required byte size and the read-only shadow consumer stays within range.
scenarios.negative_control: A small count far below every overflow boundary produces identical mathematical and machine multiplication results and a fully valid synthetic allocation.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, requires uncontrolled invalid memory access, or cannot remain synthetic and bounded.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After checked multiplication before narrowing, the truncating boundary fixture is rejected or allocated safely while the valid controls preserve behavior.
scenarios.value_unit_representation_trace: Record source count identity and generation, element units, mathematical count, machine width/signedness, byte conversion, and the narrow allocation representation.
scenarios.arithmetic_conversion_trace: Trace count times element_size in the mathematical domain, the wider machine intermediate, the truncation event, and the final allocation-domain byte value.
scenarios.check_use_domain_binding: Bind the check-domain count/size representation to the later allocation and use-domain values and identify the first point where the numeric domains diverge.
scenarios.allocation_object_usable_size: Record fake allocation request, actual fake object identity/generation, nominal size, metadata, alignment, and exact usable payload exposed to the shadow consumer.
scenarios.index_offset_stride_access_width: Bind logical element index, byte stride, derived offset, access width, exact start/end equation, and the first shadow range that exceeds usable size.
scenarios.aggregate_alignment_nested_size: Model the aggregate count × element_size expression and any header/alignment addition so every intermediate width and unit conversion is explicit.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the exact read-only shadow-range consumer that validates the logical element access against the fake object's usable byte interval.
scenarios.effective_invalid_range_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to constructing one synthetic logical access range larger than the fake object created by a truncated allocation size.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a structured shadow-memory rejection/canary receipt containing requested size, required size, offending range, and no unsafe real-memory access.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate source generation, multiplication expression, truncation, fake object generation, logical access, shadow consumer, and bounded receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold count, element size, object model, and consumer fixed while changing only truncating multiplication to checked wide multiplication and compare the range result.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject allocator rounding, hidden padding, smaller real access width, parser rejection, lifetime faults, or receipt from another object generation as explanations.
scenarios.evidence_level: BND4 because a bounded fake-object and shadow-range marker demonstrates the invalid range caused by the exact multiply-and-truncate allocation chain.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: BND4 maximum until complete provenance, alternative elimination, counterfactual replay, exact receipt binding, and remediation regression satisfy BND5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A negative synthetic length or index crosses a signed-to-unsigned conversion and is checked only after conversion, creating a mismatched size or range domain.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled read-only numeric oracle and fake range consumer record the signed value, unsigned representation, check result, and inert range decision only.
scenarios.positive_control: A non-negative synthetic value within the valid signed domain converts to the same mathematical unsigned value and passes the intended range predicate safely.
scenarios.negative_control: The same negative value rejected before unsigned conversion produces no allocation or range request and reaches no downstream fake consumer.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, requires uncontrolled invalid memory access, or cannot remain synthetic and bounded.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After validating negativity in the signed domain before conversion, negative fixtures are rejected and valid non-negative controls remain accepted.
scenarios.value_unit_representation_trace: Record source value identity/generation, signed mathematical value, units, source width, unsigned destination width, and bit-pattern-preserving conversion result.
scenarios.arithmetic_conversion_trace: Trace the signed-to-unsigned conversion, any promotion used by the comparison, the resulting machine value, and the exact check-domain representation.
scenarios.check_use_domain_binding: Show whether the implemented predicate compares the post-conversion unsigned value while the intended constraint was defined over the original signed domain.
scenarios.allocation_object_usable_size: Record any fake size request or synthetic object created from the unsigned value, including requested, actual, declared, and usable sizes if allocation occurs.
scenarios.index_offset_stride_access_width: For index paths, bind post-cast index, stride, derived offset, access width, valid interval, and inert shadow-range result for the synthetic object.
scenarios.aggregate_alignment_nested_size: Record whether the converted value participates in later multiplication, addition, or alignment and keep all intermediate widths and units explicit.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the controlled fake allocator or read-only range consumer that interprets the converted unsigned value as a size or offset.
scenarios.effective_invalid_range_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to promoting one negative synthetic semantic value into a different unsigned size/range domain under the mismatched guard.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a structured inert receipt showing signed value, unsigned representation, predicate outcome, and fake allocation/range decision.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind source generation, conversion event, check predicate, fake object/range identity, downstream consumer, and deterministic receipt in one causal record.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold the numeric bit pattern and downstream consumer constant while moving the negativity check before versus after unsigned conversion.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject language-defined safe rejection, no downstream use, allocator failure before consumption, unit mismatch elsewhere, or a different source generation as explanations.
scenarios.evidence_level: BND3 because a controlled fake consumer accepts the post-conversion value in an invalid intended range without unsafe external or real-memory effects.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: BND3 maximum until a stronger bounded invalid-range effect plus complete object/use provenance and remediation replay justify BND4 or BND5.

scenarios.hypothesis: An alignment-up calculation near a machine-width boundary wraps or truncates so the checked/requested object size is smaller than the mathematically aligned size later assumed.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A synthetic checked-alignment oracle, fake allocator, and read-only shadow region report pre-round, rounded, requested, usable, and consumed sizes without unsafe access.
scenarios.positive_control: A value safely below the alignment boundary rounds upward identically in mathematical and machine domains and produces a correctly sized fake object.
scenarios.negative_control: An already aligned small value requires no effective rounding and demonstrates that the helper preserves size when no boundary transition is involved.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, requires uncontrolled invalid memory access, or cannot remain synthetic and bounded.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After replacing wrapping alignment arithmetic with checked alignment-up, boundary inputs are rejected or sized correctly while ordinary aligned controls remain unchanged.
scenarios.value_unit_representation_trace: Record source size identity/generation, byte units, mathematical value, machine width/signedness, alignment quantum, and post-round representation.
scenarios.arithmetic_conversion_trace: Expand addend, addition, mask/division, truncation or wrap, mathematical aligned result, machine aligned result, and first divergent intermediate.
scenarios.check_use_domain_binding: Bind the size accepted by any pre-alignment check to the rounded allocation-domain size and the later consumer's assumed aligned use-domain size.
scenarios.allocation_object_usable_size: Record fake allocation request, object generation, alignment padding, actual fake capacity, and exact usable payload relative to the mathematical aligned requirement.
scenarios.index_offset_stride_access_width: Bind the downstream bounded region or final aligned field access, including offset, stride if any, access width, start/end, and valid fake interval.
scenarios.aggregate_alignment_nested_size: Treat the alignment-up expression as the primary aggregate chain and record all additions, masks, divisions, page/unit conversions, and widths.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the exact fake allocator or read-only aligned-region consumer that observes the machine-rounded size and returns an inert structured result.
scenarios.effective_invalid_range_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to one synthetic aligned range whose mathematically required size exceeds the fake object's wrapped machine size.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a shadow-range or fake-canary receipt showing pre-round size, machine rounded size, mathematical rounded size, and invalid interval.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate source generation, alignment expression, wrap/truncation event, fake object generation, consumer identity, and bounded receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold source size, alignment quantum, object model, and consumer fixed while switching only wrapping alignment-up to checked alignment-up arithmetic.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject allocator over-allocation, hidden padding, different alignment contract, smaller consumer range, sanitizer layout changes, or stale object receipts.
scenarios.evidence_level: BND4 because the fake object and shadow region demonstrate a bounded invalid aligned range directly caused by the wrapping alignment calculation.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: BND4 maximum until full arithmetic/object provenance, counterfactuals, eliminated alternatives, receipt binding, and remediation replay satisfy BND5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A bounds guard validates only that a synthetic start offset is at or below an inclusive endpoint while omitting access width, so the final read-only range crosses the exact object end.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled shadow-range consumer and fake object report start, access width, computed end, valid interval, and inert rejection/canary state without real invalid dereference.
scenarios.positive_control: The same access width starting exactly far enough before the end produces an end-exclusive range equal to object size and remains fully valid.
scenarios.negative_control: A start offset already beyond the object end is rejected by both the weak and corrected guards, confirming the fixture's basic endpoint model.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, requires uncontrolled invalid memory access, or cannot remain synthetic and bounded.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After replacing the start-only predicate with a width-aware end-range predicate, crossing accesses are rejected and exact-end valid controls remain accepted.
scenarios.value_unit_representation_trace: Record offset identity/generation, byte units, mathematical offset, integer representation, object-size representation, and access-width representation.
scenarios.arithmetic_conversion_trace: Trace any promotions plus the offset + access_width end calculation in both mathematical and machine domains and confirm no unrelated overflow is required.
scenarios.check_use_domain_binding: Bind the implemented start-offset predicate to the downstream width-aware access equation and show the omitted width creates the check/use mismatch.
scenarios.allocation_object_usable_size: Record fake object identity/generation, declared object size, any metadata or padding, exact usable payload, and region identity used by the range consumer.
scenarios.index_offset_stride_access_width: Capture start offset, stride if applicable, access width, end-exclusive equation, valid interval, one-past-end distinction, and first byte outside range.
scenarios.aggregate_alignment_nested_size: Record that no aggregate overflow or alignment defect is necessary, or explicitly document any header/unit term so endpoint reasoning stays isolated.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the exact read-only shadow consumer that evaluates the synthetic access interval and emits an inert range-crossing receipt.
scenarios.effective_invalid_range_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to one bounded synthetic access interval crossing the fake object's usable end because access width was omitted from the guard.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is an inert structured receipt naming object generation, start, width, end, valid interval, and exact range-crossing amount.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind offset generation, check predicate, object generation, access-width equation, shadow consumer, and deterministic result receipt in one causal tuple.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold object, offset, width, representation, and consumer constant while changing only start-only validation to width-aware end-range validation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject object padding, alternate endpoint convention, zero-width access, different actual access width, pointer-formation-only behavior, or another object generation.
scenarios.evidence_level: BND4 because a bounded read-only shadow range demonstrates exact endpoint crossing caused solely by the missing access-width term.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: BND4 maximum until complete check/use provenance, counterfactual controls, eliminated alternatives, receipt binding, and remediation regression reach BND5.
